speaker: An angel of the Lord, in a dream
summary: The first speech in Matthew's Gospel is an angel's, addressed to Joseph as 'son of David'.

speaker: The narrator (Matthew), quoting Isaiah
summary: The first of Matthew's 'fulfilment' formulae; the words 'they will call Him Immanuel' are Isaiah's.

speaker: A voice from heaven (God the Father)
Jesus — the Sermon on the Mount
summary: The first of the five discourses Matthew closes with 'When Jesus had finished' (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1); the crowd's reaction is reported at 7:28.

speaker: 'Some of those present' — John 12:4 names Judas Iscariot
summary: Mark keeps the objectors anonymous; John attributes the complaint to Judas and adds a motive.

speaker: Jesus
summary: 'Wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.'

speaker: Mary — the Magnificat
summary: It shares its themes with Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2:1–10. A few Old Latin manuscripts attribute it to Elizabeth.

speaker: Zechariah, father of John — the Benedictus
The serpent
summary: Genesis never calls the serpent Satan; that identification is made in Revelation 12:9 and 20:2.

speaker: The LORD God, in dialogue with the man, the woman and the serpent
God, speaking directly to Israel at Sinai
summary: Deuteronomy 5:4 stresses that the people heard these words 'face to face' before asking Moses to mediate (Exodus 20:19).

speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite — first speech
summary: Job 42:7 says the friends 'have not spoken of Me what is right'.

speaker: David (superscription); quoted by Jesus on the cross (Matthew 27:46)
An unnamed 'we' — the community confessing what the Servant bore for them
summary: The speakers shift from 'we' (53:1–6) to God (53:11–12).

speaker: Stephen, before the Sanhedrin
summary: The longest speech in Acts; Luke's summary of Israel's history from Abraham to Solomon.

speaker: Paul, at the Areopagus in Athens
summary: Quotes Aratus, Phaenomena 5 (17:28b), introduced 'as some of your own poets have said'.
